sentences.text: JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated that on 13.08.2023 at about 8.30a.m, the Petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-4278 from Nandini Layout Outer Ring Road, Goraguntepalya Junction towards Sumanahalli Bridge near Dr.Rajkumar Smaraka, Nandini Layout, Bangalore.

When he reached near Dr.Rajkumar Samadhi, Nandini layout, Bengaluru, the driver of a goods carrier bearing Reg. No.KA-52-1604 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) had parked the said vehicle without any designated parking space or display of hazard signals.
As a result, the petitioner, unable to notice the stationery goods carrier in time, collided with its rear portion 3.

Due to the impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was immediately taken to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital Nandini layout,, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 13.08.2023 to 18.08.2023 and underwent surgery.
4. As a consequence of the accident, the petitioner is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
He claims to have incurred an expenditure of over Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment, medication, conveyance and incidental charges.
5. At the time of accident, Petitioner was 26 years, working as a Labourer and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- P.M. owing to the injuries, he has lost his earning capacity and livelihood.
It is therefore contended that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner seeks compensation from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of offending vehicle.
6. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

7. Respondent No.2- Insurance company has filed its written statement and denied all the averments of the petition inter alia contending that the owner of the offending vehicle and the police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

It has denied the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident and contended that the driver of the alleged offending vehicle and rider of the motorcycle were not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
He has contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner himself.
It has further stated that the alleged accident occurred on 13-8-2023, whereas the complaint was lodged only on 16-6-2023, indicating a delay of three days in reporting the incident.

The police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet against the petitioner alleging that the Rakshith B N vs Eranna V on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100822900/
2 accident occurred due to negligence on his part.

The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
On these grounds, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 13.08.2023 at about 8.30 a.m., near Dr,Rajkumar Samadhi, on Nandini Layout, Outer Ring Road, Gurguntepaqlya Junction towards Sumanhalli Bridge, he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident,
while he was riding his motorcycle bearing No. KA-06-HN-4278, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the goods carrier bearing No.KA- 52-1604?.

2.Whether the respondent No.2 proves that, the policy conditions are violated by respondent No.1 and the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation if any, how much, from whom?
3. What order or award?

two witness examined as PW-2 and PW-3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.19.

2. Civil Appeal No(s).

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the Negative Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative.

3 13. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 13.08.2023 at about 8.30a.m, the Petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 06-HN-4278 from Nandini Layout Outer Ring Road, Goraguntepalya Junction towards Sumanahalli Bridge near Dr.Rajkumar Smaraka,
Nandini Layout, Bangalore.

When he reached near Dr.Rajkumar Samadhi, Nandini layout,
Bengaluru, the driver of the offending vehicle had parked the said vehicle without any designated parking space or display of hazard signals.
As a result, the petitioner, unable to notice the stationery goods carrier in time, collided with its rear portion.

Due to the impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was immediately taken to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital Nandini layout,, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 13.08.2023 to 18.08.2023 and underwent surgery.
14. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1.

PW-1 has produced true copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, Complaint at Ex.P.2, spot mahazar at Ex.P3, spot sketch at Ex.P.4, Notice U/Sec.133 MV Act at Ex.P5, Reply U/Sec.133 of MV Act at Ex.P6, IMV report at Ex.P.7, wound certificate at Ex.P.8 and charge sheet a/w statements at Ex.P.9, Notarized copy of Aadhaar card &
DL of petitioner at Ex.P10 & 11, Discharge summary at Ex.P12, Medical bill at Ex.P13.

Further,
Manith Kumar was examined as PW-2 and he has produced 4 documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P17 and Dr.Nagaraj B.N., was examined as PW-3 and he has produced the 2 documents at Ex.P.18 and Ex.P.19.
15.
As per Ex. P 8 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained a traumatic brain injury, multiple facial bone fracture & a right distal radius fracture.
It is stated that these injuries are grievous in nature.

16. The respondent No.2 examined its official as RW-1, who deposed that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and further stated that the charge sheet was filed against the petitioner.
It was contended that the petitioner contributed to the cause of the accident by riding his motorcycle at high speed and in a rash and negligent thereby causing the accident.

RW-1 also produced the insurance policy, which is marked at Ex.R.2.
17.
During the course of cross examination, a suggestion was put to PW1 that the accident occurred due to his negligence.
PW1 denied the suggestion.
However, he admitted that after investigation,the charge sheet was filed against him, alleging that the accident was a result of his negligence.
He denied riding the vehicle at high speed and further denied the suggestion that the accident could have been avoided had he observed the vehicle carefully and following traffic rules.
18. There is no serious dispute regarding the occurrence of accident and the fact that the petitioner sustained injuries as a result of the said accident.
The documents on record indicate that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence both on the part of the petitioner and driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver had parked the goods vehicle improperly, without any designated parking space or display of hazard signals.
Consequently, the petitioner, unable to notice the stationery goods carrier in time, collided with its rear portion.
As per Ex.P 7 IMV report to show that there is no mechanical defect in the offending vehicle.
Rajajinagar Traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.431/2023 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 283 and 337 of IPC against the petitioner as well as the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the the driver of the offending vehicle had parked the vehicle without any designated parking space or display of hazard signals.
As a result, the petitioner, unable to notice the stationery goods carrier in time, collided with its rear portion.
Therefore, it is contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
20. It is evident from the material on record that the negligence of both parties the petitioner and the driver of the offending vehicle led to the accident.
The petitioner has sought to emphasize that the driver of the offending vehicle failed to park in a proper location and did not display appropriate hazard signals.

On the other hand, Respondent no 2, in its written statement and through the testimony of RW1, has contended that the petitioner was riding his motorcycle at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, thereby causing the accident.
21.

From the overall evidence and the manner in which the accident occurred, this tribunal is of the view that both the petitioner and the driver of the offending vehicle were negligent, and accordingly,
contributory negligence must be attributed to the petitioner as well as the driver of the offending vehicle.
22.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle exercised caution and refrained from parking the vehicle at the alleged location, the accident could likely have been avoided.
However, it is also observed that the petitioner, despite being aware of traffic rules, was riding the motorcycle at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner.
There is no proper explanation provided by the petitioner as to why he was riding in such a manner.
The evidence indicates that the accident and resulting injuries were caused due to over speed on the part of the petitioner.
23. As I have already discussed that there is no material to show that the accident occurred in the middle of the road or during the hours of darkness.
Therefore, the facts and circumstances of the present case are distinguishable and the principles laid down in the decisions relied upon by the petitioners are not applicable to this case.
24. Thus the facts and circumstances suggest contributory negligence on the part of both the driver of the offending vehicle and the petitioner.

If the petitioner had not been riding at such high speed,
he could have controlled the motorcycle and possibly avoided the accident.
Considering all these aspects, it is just and proper to hold that the both the driver of offending vehicle and the petitioner equally contributed to the cause of the accident.
Therefore, liability is apportioned at 50% each between them.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.2:-
The respondent No.2 has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

However, on reading of entire material,
there is no evidence placed before the court to substantiate that the respondent no 1 committed any such violation.
It is evident that the offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy at time of the accident.
Wherefore, the liability to compensate the petitioners rest with the respondent No.1.
hence I answer issue no 2 in the negative.

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.3 :-As per Ex.P.8 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained a traumatic brain injury, multiple facial bone fracture & aright distal radius fracture.

He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as Labourer and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

28. Manith Kumar, MRO at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital was examined as PW-2 and he has produced 4 documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P17.
29. PW-3
Dr.Nagaraj B.N.., an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho And Dental center, deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and was treated at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru.
The Petitioner suffered traumatic brain injury, multiple facial bone fracture and a right distal radius fracture.
He underwent open reduction and internal fixation ORIF for the left lefort II Fracture, lip reconstruction and advancement flap.
The distal radius fracture was managed conservatively.
30. PW-3 examined the Petitioner both clinically and radiologically while assessing disability.

During the examination, the petitioner complained of an inability to lift weights with his right hand,
persistent pain, and weakness in the same hand.
Swelling and restricted movement of the right wrist.
PW3 assessed the whole body disability at 11%.
in his cross-examination has stated that he has not treated the Petitioner.
He stated that radius fracture was treated conservatively.
Injuries had healed.
The petitioner however, stated he underwent surgery.

EX P12 discharge summary reveals that the petitioner underwent ORIF of left lefort II fracture with plating and screws fixation, along with lip reconstruction and advancement flap cover done under GA on 14.05.2023.
32. It is pertinent to note that PW2 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, considering that the grievous injury and difficulties and evidence of PW-3,
avocation and the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 8%.
33. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 26 years.

Ex.P.10 and 11- Aadhar card DL shows that he was born on 29.05.1997, the same is considered as age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 26 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 17.
34.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injury.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

However,
the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.

sentences.text: The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
36. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of injury, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
The Petitioner is working as Labourer

,
considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 8%.

Thus, loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 17 x 8 /100= Rs.2,61,120/-
towards loss of future income.
37. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and was treated as inpatient,
which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .20,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
38. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is suffering from difficulties to do his day today activities and face hardships.

Hence, Petitioner is awarded .15,000/-
under loss of amenities of life.
39. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.13 amounting to Rs.3,74,824/-.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of .3,74,824 /- towards Medical Expenses.
40. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P-12 - Discharge summary shows that, Petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital from 13.08.2023 to 18.08.2023 i.e., for 6 days.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .10,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
41. Loss of earning during laid up period:
With regard to loss of earnings during treatment, around 1 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 1 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 1 = 16,000/-.
42.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,48,472/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank of his choice for a period of 2 years.
